items.item_text: Basic Life Support - CPR - authorized by the American Heart Association
1-3 years 2 years minimum acute care experience,with 1 year of critical care experience. If no qualified candidate, may consider training positions, depending on staffing needs
Pulmonary Function testing, arterial bloodgas quality control and bronchoscopy experience

Analyzes blood specimens for pH, pCO2, pO2 and THb with no more than 5 errors per year. Demonstrates competence in recognizing and reporting critical values in the pediatric, adult and geriatric patient.
Performs bronchoscopies and maintains records per procedure with a high degree of accuracy as demonstrated by < 5% error
Performs PFT exams accurately with < 10 errors per year as demonstrated by reporting erroneous data or having to recall patients to correct test data
Performs QC tests on blood gas analyzers, performs and maintains department QC and quality metrics such as daily crash cart checks and bronchoscope cleaning audits.< 5% per year per audit

Performs other procedures such as indirect calorimetry, HAST, ambulations and any other procedures requested with <5% errors per year, as demonstrated by reporting physiologically erroneous data1.6 Evaluates Blood Gas results for completeness and footnoting of critical values. Notifies therapists of their deficiencies
Maintains accurate records and billing in the electronic health record with < 5% error as demonstrated by audit.
Completion of an AMA approved respiratory therapy program
Registered by the National Board of Respiratory Care as a Registered Respiratory Therapist (RRT) preferred
